decision_reason: CC-CAP-001 requires a const-alias equality unit test; the schema has no separate `unit` verifier, so the lane is routed through `proptest` with a degenerate strategy (PROPTEST_CASES=10, prop_assert_eq!(MAX_TRIM_KEY_LEN, JOURNAL_KEY_BYTES) and prop_assert_eq!(MAX_SNAPSHOT_KEY_LEN, JOURNAL_KEY_BYTES)). The literal 17 is replaced by JOURNAL_KEY_BYTES at the alias site, so the const chain enforces compile-time equality. Source: crates/vb_storage/src/constants.rs lines 74-79.

CC-CAP-005 requires the existing test journal_error_trim_wrapper_delegates_incomplete_trim_code at crates/vb_storage/src/error_code_tests.rs:~246 to continue to assert the 0x4102 propagation through JournalError::Trim(inner). The diagnostic code is INCOMPLETE_TRIM_CODE (line 62 of trimming/mod.rs); JournalError::Trim(inner).diagnostic_code() delegates to inner.diagnostic_code() (error/codes.rs:167). Routed through `proptest` verifier vocabulary because the schema has no separate `unit` verifier; the test is cargo-test-style.

CC-CAP-002/003/004 demand an arbitrary-length key generator over the snapshot prefix. The proptest exercises the full length space 0..=256 with PROPTEST_CASES=10000 and asserts the only Ok(Some(seq)) path is length == 17 with a valid RunSnapshot decode; all other lengths yield Err(TrimError::IncompleteTrim { .. }) with the typed 0x4102 error code. Property pressure is the canonical lane for hostile_input + bounded_state per references/risk-taxonomy.md (parser/codec, rejection, property tags).

CC-CAP-002/003/004/009/010 demand integration tests that plant malformed raw keys via journal.run_snapshot.insert(...) / journal.events.insert(...) using temp_journal() to spin up a real Fjall instance. Existing tests at snapshot_tests.rs:208-248 (Round 10 issue 7 regression, 13-byte planted key) and trimming/tests.rs:875-987 (SC-006 + CC-002, 9-byte planted keys) are the regression gate. CC-CAP-010 adds three new overlong cases (24 bytes). Routed through `proptest` verifier vocabulary because the schema has no separate `integration` verifier; the test is cargo-test-style with PROPTEST_CASES=1.

CC-CAP-008 requires moon run :lint-src (Holzman Rust zero-tolerance source lint per .moon/tasks/all.yml:46-62) plus cargo check --workspace to pass with zero changes outside vb_storage. CC-CAP-009 requires the existing tests at snapshot_tests.rs:208-248 and trimming/tests.rs:875-987 to continue to pass. The literal-replacement invariant (magic 17 -> MAX_TRIM_KEY_LEN / MAX_SNAPSHOT_KEY_LEN at trimming/logic.rs:36, 77, 222) is verified by rg -n 'key\.len\(\) != 17' crates/vb_storage/src/trimming/logic.rs returning no matches (anti-invariant). Routed through `proptest` verifier vocabulary because the schema has no separate `clippy` or `lint` verifier.

The only non-trivial bound is a usize const alias to another usize const literal; verifying a const against itself is vacuous (no exec fn, no loop, no arithmetic). The const alias chain (MAX_TRIM_KEY_LEN = JOURNAL_KEY_BYTES; MAX_SNAPSHOT_KEY_LEN = JOURNAL_KEY_BYTES) is a compile-time invariant enforced by the `const X = Y` syntax and discharged by cargo check. Adding a Kani harness would only verify the alias equality, which the compiler already discharges. Sources: crates/vb_storage/src/constants.rs lines 74-79 (declaration site only); no production exec fn is added.

No new exec fn is introduced by this bead; the existing TrimError::IncompleteTrim { deleted_count: u64 } variant at trimming/mod.rs:51-54 is preserved verbatim and its 0x4102 code (INCOMPLETE_TRIM_CODE at line 62) is already covered by error_code_tests.rs:~246. The bead is a numeric/cap refinement, not a functional invariant; Verus is the right tool for Rust-local functional invariants, not for const alias equality. Sources: crates/vb_storage/src/trimming/mod.rs:51-54 (existing variant); no new exec fn at any call site.

The cap is a usize const alias; refining a usize value already discharged by `const X = JOURNAL_KEY_BYTES` adds no information. Flux's SMT-decidable fragment is targeted at refinement types (e.g., `Offset stays within [0, LEN)`) and `#[refined_by]` / `#[sig]` expressions, not at const equality. The contract (CC-CAP-001) commits to a unit-test proof with PROPTEST_CASES=10, not a Flux refinement. Source: crates/vb_storage/src/constants.rs lines 74-79; no runtime refinement target is in scope.

Key encoders (run_event_key at crates/vb_storage/src/keys.rs:81, run_snapshot_key at crates/vb_storage/src/keys.rs:86) are pure 1-input=1-output ArrayVec<u8, JOURNAL_KEY_BYTES> writes; the return type is fixed-size [u8; 17], so fuzzing the encoder adds no coverage beyond the proptest length roundtrip on PO-003-PROPTEST. The decoders (decode_storage_key at keys.rs:346, decode_run_event_key at keys.rs:451) already enforce length equality via KeyDecodeError::KeyLengthMismatch; their hostile-input surface is covered by the proptest length roundtrip and the integration tests on PO-002-INTEGRATION. No parser-with-arbitrary-byte-input is added by this bead.

The trim scanners (latest_durable_snapshot_seq at crates/vb_storage/src/trimming/logic.rs:26, trim_events_for_run at line 49, count_trimmable_events at line 208) are synchronous, single-threaded, and operate on a per-journal Fjall snapshot (Database::snapshot() at line 214). There is no Send/Sync boundary, no spawn, no async, no shared mutable state across threads. Loom's schedule exploration is for interleavings across threads; the trim path has no interleavings to model. The constraint is also enforced by crates/vb_storage/src/lib.rs (no tokio, no async, no threads).
